title: Dynamical Inclination and Wind Braking in Isolated Pulsar Spin-Down: Deriving the Effective Braking Index and Validity Domain
abstract: The mature idea established that systematic deviations from the canonical braking index n=3 in isolated pulsars can be explained by a unified torque model incorporating time-varying magnetic inclination angle decay and relativistic wind braking, restricted to characteristic ages > 10^4 yr and surface fields < 10^13 G. A key limitation of this initial model is that the precise functional forms of the dynamical inclination angle alpha(t) and wind braking efficiency eta(t), and their exact analytical impact on the effective braking index n_eff, remained underspecified. We refine this framework by explicitly introducing alpha(t) and eta(t) into the spin-down torque equation. We derive n_eff as an analytical function of these dynamical parameters and explicitly bound the validity domain in the (P, Pdot, B) parameter space where this relaxed torque model applies, strictly avoiding the introduction of new mechanism families beyond inclination decay and wind braking.
method: 1. Formulate the generalized spin-down torque equation by explicitly incorporating the dynamical magnetic inclination angle alpha(t) and the time-dependent relativistic wind braking efficiency eta(t). 2. Analytically derive the effective braking index n_eff as a function of alpha(t), eta(t), and their time derivatives, repairing the underspecified torque dynamics of the mature model. 3. Map the derived n_eff to observable pulsar parameters to establish the explicit validity domain in the (P, Pdot, B) space where the relaxed torque model holds. 4. Verify the model by comparing the derived n_eff bounds against observed braking indices of isolated pulsars, confirming that deviations from n=3 are fully captured by inclination decay and wind braking without requiring ad hoc magnetic field decay or binary recycling mechanisms.
introduction: Pulsars, the rapidly rotating neutron stars born from the core collapse of massive stars, serve as critical laboratories for extreme physics. Their formation and subsequent evolution bifurcate into two primary pathways: isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down and binary recycling accompanied by companion ablation. Distinguishing these mechanisms is essential for understanding the mass-spin relation of massive neutron stars, yet current theoretical frameworks often rely on standard static equation of state (EoS) axioms that fail to formally unify these evolutionary channels. Building on the insights of recent long-term timing analyses, such as the study of SAX J1808.4-3658, which reveals significant quiescent spin-down and large orbital period derivatives indicative of companion ablation, it is evident that binary interactions profoundly alter neutron star evolution. However, a critical mechanism explanation gap remains: standard EoS formulations do not adequately account for the rotational and thermal support provided by binary mass accretion, leaving the formation of massive neutron stars (>2.0 M_sun) via recycling mechanisms theoretically underspecified. This proposal refines a mature unified torque model by explicitly incorporating dynamical magnetic inclination angle decay and relativistic wind braking to derive the effective braking index as an analytical function of these parameters. We rigorously bound the validity domain in the (P, Pdot, B) parameter space, strictly avoiding ad hoc magnetic field decay. By replacing standard static equilibrium EoS axioms with relaxed axioms that formally integrate binary recycling and companion ablation, we aim to derive a distinct mechanism-mass-spin relation, thereby resolving the ambiguity between isolated and binary formation pathways for massive neutron stars.

directions.title: Unifying Isolated Spin-Down and Binary Recycling in Massive Neutron Star Formation via Relaxed Equation of State Axioms
directions.abstract: The formation of massive neutron stars requires distinguishing isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down from binary recycling mechanisms. Current static equation of state axioms fail to unify these pathways for masses exceeding the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) limit. We relax the static equilibrium axioms of the dense matter equation of state to formally incorporate the rotational and thermal support provided by binary mass accretion and companion ablation. This yields a unified pulsar evolution formal model and a novel mechanism-mass-spin relation. By mathematically verifying this framework, we establish the validity domain where massive neutron stars emerge from binary recycling rather than isolated collapse, resolving the mechanism explanation gap for dense matter equations of state.

hypothesis.intervention_or_transformation: Replacing standard static equilibrium equation of state axioms with relaxed axioms that permit higher mass limits via the rotational and thermal support of binary mass accretion.
hypothesis.expected_mechanism: The relaxed static equilibrium axioms mathematically allow for mass accumulation beyond the isolated static Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit by formally incorporating the centrifugal support and thermal pressure from binary accretion, explaining the existence of massive pulsars through binary recycling.

Binary mass accretion and angular momentum transfer can be modeled as a continuous thermodynamic and mechanical perturbation that modifies the effective equilibrium conditions of the neutron star.
